value.body: A sports coach trains athletes in one sport, from beginners to competitive players. Employers include private academies, schools, clubs, and the training centres of the Sports Authority of India and state sports departments. Days are mostly on the field or court, often early mornings and evenings, with planning and athlete monitoring in between.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Physical education degree plus a coaching diploma or federation licence

items.label: What counts
items.value: Your own playing record in the sport

items.label: B.P.Ed enrolment
items.note: Bachelor of Physical Education, all modes; ~32% women

items.label: B.P.Ed out-turn
items.note: Graduates passing out, based on actual responses

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many coaches start as assistant coaches at academies or schools while earning a coaching qualification. Government coach posts with SAI or state departments are filled when notified and usually ask for a recognised coaching diploma and a sports record.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Technique and tactics of your sport

value.title: At a glance
items: Income often depends on the academy or number of trainees.
Government coach posts are few and often on contract.
Next roles: head coach, academy director, team coach at state level.

value.title: B.P.Ed enrolment
value.note: Bachelor of Physical Education only, all modes. Not every graduate becomes a coach; many teach physical education in schools.
